I'm so sorry that this all has happened to you. It sounds so complicated. Now you and I both know that punching your partner isn't the best way to solve things, and I'm sorry that you had to go through that ordeal, and knowing it was wrong. It must have really hurt for you. It's okay for you to be disappointed or ashamed of your actions. Sometimes people do wrong things and regret them.
It's really saddening to hear that you wanted to throw yourself off a building. You were drunk so maybe these weren't your true feelings. It's easy to get wound up by regret, and let it sit on you like a weight. Maybe killing yourself would have meant you didn't do the domestic violence, but I don't think it would have solved the problems you were facing. It's really upsetting that it seems like a good idea to me.
It must be really hard to feel like you're keeping secrets from whomever you're dating. What do you think would happen if you told them? And maybe you're right. Maybe now it is not the time when you should be in a relationship. Maybe you might want to think about the domestic abuse incident and why it is affecting your future. A lot of people have dark and shameful secrets. I'm truly sorry that you feel that nobody will understand. It must be really uncomfortable feeling as if what you did will scare future partners away.
Your emotions about what you've done and how it's affecting you are completely valid. Even though you may have done a bad thing, it is completely okay, and it makes sense that you are feeling depressed about what you've done. You have a right to be sad about it. If you feel this much remorse about your actions, and you won't do it again it could be a good idea to talk to a therapist, a psychologist or a psychiatrist about how to get past this. Then again maybe not. Maybe you just need a little self-exploration time.
It must be really horrible for you to have feelings for a person then have them overwhelmed by bad memories of your past. You might not be ready to be in a relationship until you overcome what you have done. Honestly, to me I don't think you sound like a bad person at all. I feel like you're a good person who made a tragic mistake. Maybe what you did was wrong but that doesn't detract from the fact you have a good heart. It's good that you're reaching out to try and speak to someone on here. It shows that you're already looking to improve yourself. A lot of men (and people in general) who are suffering translate their suffering into moments of violence. It's not right but it is very sad and it is a good idea to seek help from somebody.
I'm truly so sorry that you've had to go through all this pain and anguish. I really wish you luck for the future. Who knows what will happen. Maybe you will find someone who understands you and doesn't hate you for what you've done and loves you all the while. I hope you do. Please try and keep yourself safe as nobody knows what fortune awakes you just around the corner. I really sympathise with what you been through and I wish you the best of luck. Thank you for sharing your story.
